free_tier: free, no API key; the award-search endpoint is POST-only
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - no published numeric limit found; the 20-request probe at a 0.9 s interval was never throttled
licence: US federal government work, public domain in the US (17 U.S.C. 105); API documentation at api.usaspending.gov
update_frequency: daily (documented); not verified in this probe
historical_coverage: federal awards from FY2008 onward, FPDS-derived
entity_identifiers: Award ID (agency PIID, not globally unique)
recipient_id / recipient UEI field (available on the award detail endpoint)
recipient name string (token-searchable, NOT an identifier)
timestamp_fields: Period of Performance Current End Date
known_limitations: NO publication clock: the API publishes action/signature/performance dates but not the date an award first became publicly visible. source_public_at therefore cannot be taken from this source without an explicit, flagged approximation; event_at (signature or performance start) must not be relabelled as publication.
Start Date is the period-of-performance start, NOT a public-visibility date. Using it as source_public_at would fabricate look-ahead.
Awards only: federal award actions from FPDS. There is no pre-award tender/notice record, so the notice->award step of the procurement chain cannot be built here; only award->contract-value.
No product/device identifier anywhere in the schema. Contract `Description` is free text written by contracting officers; keyword hits in it are not a product link and must not be treated as one.

recipient_search_text is a token search, not an exact entity match. In the five-firm probe 'GE HealthCare' returned CHANGE HEALTHCARE TECHNOLOGIES LLC and related entities; only 1 of 10 first-page names resolved to GE HealthCare.
spending_by_award_count with a recipient token is an upper bound on 'names containing these tokens', not a count of awards to the firm.
Amounts are federal obligations, not supplier revenue; obligations can be de-obligated later and do not equal recognised revenue.
Subcontracting relationships are not exposed, so a distributor sale through a prime contractor is invisible.
bulk_download_available is a documentation claim (the USASpending download centre advertises award archives); the archive itself was NOT probed in this pass.
research_value: Gives MedRadar the US federal demand side for the five target firms at award granularity, with recipient names, obligating agency and obligation amounts. It is the only verified source in this batch that both names the winning supplier and publishes a machine-readable award amount for US federal contracts, so it supports 'public money actually awarded to firm X' claims - provided the award is not equated with revenue.
cost_notes: free; no key, no account, no quota observed
